From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-04-20T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx errors impacting inference calls

Quick preliminary RCA (work in progress):
- Signal: 09:04–09:20 UTC spike in kernel-level context-switches on the GPU hosts serving this model variant.
- Root cause (probable): An autoscaling policy change rolled out last night increased batch aggregation thresholds for lower-cost instances. Under a bursty traffic pattern from Bridgestone's route we saw larger-than-expected batch sizes causing memory pressure and an unoptimized kernel fallback path that increases token latency and occasional OOM-triggered retries (reported as 5xx).
- Immediate mitigations performed:
  1) Rolled back the batching threshold change for the affected pool at 09:28 UTC.
  2) Forced per-request concurrency to 1 for Bridgestone's route as a temporary SLO-preserving measure.

Evidence attached: kernel dumps and a short trace. Working on a concise RCA doc.

Attachment: kernel_dumps.zip
Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batching-fallback

Karthik

Status summary:
- Incident began: ~09:04 UTC
- Primary impact: latency up to ~3.2s p50 -> 7s p95; 5xx rate peaked at 12%
- Mitigation: rollback of batching threshold and temporary per-request concurrency enforced (service restored progressively by 09:35 UTC)
- Customer impact: checkout retries observed; we estimate ~2.8% conversion impact during the window — CS will quantify.

Action plan & owners (short):
- RCA doc + technical deep-dive: Karthik (deliver by EOD 2028-04-21)

- Customer remediation: Marissa (credits & SLA remediation proposal by 2028-04-21)
- Exec readout: 16:00 UTC today — Soojin to lead; Jordan to present impact and next steps.
